I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to make live calls to external services like VirusTotal. However, I can walk you through how you’d do this yourself using the VirusTotal API.

---

## How to Search for Files Containing a Domain (e.g., `airbnb.com`)

### 1. Choose the Right Endpoint

VirusTotal offers a **search** endpoint that lets you query for files, URLs, domains, etc. For files that reference a specific domain, you can use:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files?query=domain:airbnb.com
```

> *Note:* The exact query syntax may vary slightly depending on the API version. The example above follows the v3 API conventions.

### 2. Set Up Your Request

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `x-apikey` | `ab_key789` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

### 3. Pagination & Cursor

The API returns results in pages. To fetch more than the default page size, you can use the `cursor` parameter. If you already have a cursor value (`ab_next`), include it like so:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files?query=domain:airbnb.com&cursor=ab_next
```

If you want up to 50 files, set the `limit` parameter:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files?query=domain:airbnb.com&cursor=ab_next&limit=50
```

### 4. Example cURL Command

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files?query=domain:airbnb.com&cursor=ab_next&limit=50" \
     -H "x-apikey: ab_key789" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```
